tone.target: dry 60s folk-rock electric with clean-to-edge breakup and bright chime
tone.profile: dry 60s folk-rock electric with clean-to-edge breakup and bright chime
tone.summary: A classic 60s folk-rock chain utilizing a clean boost for chime, followed by a vintage British amp model (UK SLP) paired with a smaller cabinet (US 2x12) to achieve bright, dry, edge-of-breakup tones.

rig.name: Buffalo Springfield - For What It's Worth - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide a clean, bright boost to enhance the 'chime' and strummed attack without adding grit.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used as a transparent volume/tone enhancer, mimicking a clean pedal like an early Vox booster.

blocks.purpose: Keep the signal clean and avoid modern drive or fuzz.
Simulate the clean, bright tone of a vintage British/American combo amp (Vox/Fender vibe) while maintaining headroom.
blocks.gap: The UK SLP is chosen for its classic, non-aggressive voicing suitable for 60s folk tones.

blocks.purpose: Mimic the smaller, brighter sound of a 1x12 or 2x12 cabinet favored by Tele/Strat players.
blocks.gap: The US 2x12 provides the necessary bright and focused character without sounding overly massive.

blocks.purpose: Brighten the high end and slightly scoop the low-mids to enhance chime and clarity.
blocks.gap: Used for surgical tone shaping, crucial for achieving that 'bright strummed attack'.

blocks.purpose: Keep the tone natural and avoid wah effects.
Avoid modulation effects to maintain a dry, natural 60s sound.
Provide a subtle, natural room ambience without sounding heavy or modern.
blocks.gap: The Room reverb is used sparingly to meet the 'light room only' requirement.

improvements.summary: Refine cabinet and room simulation for a drier, brighter 60s folk-rock sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance the bright, focused chime and dry character of early 60s recordings.
